deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 35 is a continuous page of lecture notes on ancient history, written in German Kurrent. It belongs to the same sequence as folios 34 and 36. The scheme (periods of Carthaginian history, then 'Zweiter Abschnitt: Geschichte des persischen Reichs 560–330') matches the standard Göttingen ancient-history course of A. H. L. Heeren (Handbuch der Geschichte der Staaten des Alterthums). The hand and content suggest a student's lecture transcript bound into the bundle, not a Gauss autograph. Nothing on the page is a derivation, calculation or mathematical remark.

Content, step by step:
(1) End of the second period of Carthaginian history (480–264 BC). Syracuse is ruled by Gelon. On the same day as the Persian defeat at Salamis, the great Carthaginian army (under Hamilcar) is destroyed. This is the battle of Himera, 480 BC. Carthage must pay 2000 talents. The writer glosses: '1 Talent ist nach hiesigem Gelde 1400 rt', i.e. 1 talent = 1400 Reichsthaler in local money. This is the only numerical aside; it is a currency conversion, not a computation.
(2) From 410 BC new Carthaginian wars in Sicily begin. 'Hamilcar' goes again with 100000 men, is successful and takes several cities. The Syracusans, in great danger, make Dionysius their leader. Four wars are fought with Dionysius I, 405–368.
(3) New section 'Zweiter Abschnitt, Geschichte des VIII persischen Reichs von 560–330'. The empire was founded by a nomadic people but soon gained great extent and higher culture. Its founder and first head is Cyrus. The Persians were inhabitants of the region Persis: a rough, warlike mountain people with a tribal constitution. The nation was divided into 10 tribes, distinguished by rank and way of life. The list continues on f. 36: 3 noble or warrior tribes led by the Pasargadae, 3 agricultural tribes, 4 nomadic tribes (after Herodotus I.125).

The only implicit arithmetic (mine, not on the page): the indemnity of 2000 talents × 1400 rt = 2,800,000 Reichsthaler. The writer does not carry this out.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: the Carthaginian commander of the 410/409 BC Sicilian expedition was Hannibal Mago (grandson of the Hamilcar who fell at Himera), not Hamilcar. The notes say 'Hamilcar'. The figure of 100000 men follows the inflated ancient numbers (Ephorus/Diodorus).
The synchronism of Himera with Salamis follows Herodotus (VII.166). Diodorus instead synchronizes it with Thermopylae. This is a source choice rather than a slip.
Dionysius I ruled 405–367 BC. The '368' is within the usual range of his last war (c. 368/367), so this is acceptable.
The equation 1 talent = 1400 Reichsthaler is a lecturer's rough modern equivalent. Values in the literature of the period vary considerably; it cannot be judged exact.

results.what: Lecture notes on ancient history: Carthage–Syracuse wars (Himera 480 BC, the 2000-talent indemnity, wars with Dionysius I) and the beginning of the history of the Persian Empire (560–330 BC, Cyrus, Persis, ten Persian tribes)
results.modern_name: Not mathematics; standard Göttingen ancient-history curriculum (Heeren's 'Staaten des Alterthums' scheme)
results.usually_credited_to: A. H. L. Heeren (lectures/handbook, 1799 ff.), drawing on Herodotus and Diodorus

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics at all. It is routine student-style lecture notes on ancient history, probably not even in Gauss's hand. It has no bearing on the history of mathematics, beyond showing that non-mathematical material is bound into this bundle.

checkable.asserts: The 2000-talent indemnity at the stated rate of 1400 Reichsthaler per talent equals 2,800,000 Reichsthaler (implicit, not computed on the page).
The span of the four wars with Dionysius I as given (405–368 BC) is 37 years.
The stated duration of the Persian Empire (560–330 BC) is 230 years.
The ten Persian tribes split as 3 noble + 3 agricultural + 4 nomadic (completed on f. 36), consistent with the '10 Stämme' on this page.

transcription_corrections: The heading reads 'Zweiter Abschnitt / Geschichte des / VIII persischen Reichs von / 560 — 380' or '560 — 330'. The last digit group is written somewhat ambiguously in the image. 330 is historically correct and is likely what is meant.
Line 1: 'beherrscht vom König Gelon' is correct. 'Gelon' is underlined in the manuscript.
Line 6: 'Hamilcar' appears in the image as 'Hamilcal'/'Hamilcar' with a cursive final letter; the reading 'Hamilcar' is acceptable.
The opening of the Persian section ('Ehemals durch ein nomadisches Volk gestiftet') is uncertain. The first word could also be read 'Ebenso' or 'Erstens'; the image is ambiguous.
'Der Stifter dieses Reichs war Cyrus' is uncertain. The name is not clearly legible in the image, but Cyrus is confirmed by context on f. 36.
'Landschaft Persis' fits the image reasonably ('Landschaft' clearly, followed by a short word ending in -s).
The rest of the machine transcription agrees with the image to the extent legible: '2000 Talente', '1400 rt', '410', '100000 Mann', 'Dionysius dem I', '4 Kriege', '405 — 368', '10 Stämme'.
